title: Undelivered Parcel Address Link
summary: You receive a text claiming your courier delivery is held at the depot due to an incomplete house number. A link asks for a ₹25 address update fee.

messages.body: Your package #IN882910 could not be delivered: Missing building number. Please update details and pay ₹25 redelivery charge within 12h: swiftpost-track.click/addr
redFlags: Sent from personal 10-digit number instead of official SMS header (e.g., IX-INPOST)

actions.label: Inspect sender number & tracking link
actions.commentary: You checked who sent it and noticed it was sent from a personal prepaid SIM, not postal services.

actions.label: Tap the link to pay ₹25 and update address
actions.commentary: You opened the link directly from an SMS message.

actions.label: Ignore and delete the message
actions.commentary: You recognized the classic parcel scam and did not engage.

hints.nudge: Look closely at the sender. Does India Post or standard couriers send SMS from 10-digit personal mobile numbers?
hints.explain: Postal and legitimate courier services send updates from alphanumeric headers (like BZ-POST), never random mobile numbers. They never charge a re-delivery fee over a link.
hints.showMe: Choose 'Inspect sender number & tracking link' or verify tracking directly on the official courier portal.

page.heading: Official Postal Advisory
page.body: PUBLIC ADVISORY: Postal services never demand address update fees or OTPs via SMS. Never click on shortened or suspicious links.

actions.label: Block the number and report scam
actions.commentary: You verified with the official advisory and blocked the scammer.

hints.nudge: Now that you confirmed it is fake, protect yourself by blocking the number.
hints.explain: Blocking prevents further follow-up phishing attempts from this burner number.
hints.showMe: Tap 'Block the number and report scam'.

page.heading: Redelivery Fee Payment — SwiftPost
page.body: Enter Card Number, Expiry, CVV, and Net Banking Password to authorise ₹25 redelivery fee.

actions.label: Enter card details & CVV to pay ₹25
actions.commentary: You submitted your debit card number and CVV on an unencrypted fake page.

actions.label: Notice insecure HTTP & close browser immediately
actions.commentary: You realized the page was insecure and was asking for sensitive card PINs.

hints.nudge: Notice the web address. Is it an official domain? Why would an address update ask for your card PIN?
hints.explain: A genuine delivery company does not need your card CVV or ATM PIN to update an address.
hints.showMe: Tap 'Notice insecure HTTP & close browser immediately'.

saferChoices: Always check the SMS header: official couriers use verified alphanumeric sender tags (e.g. DZ-DELHIV).
Never pay nominal redelivery fees (₹5, ₹10, ₹25) via SMS links; this is a known trick to capture card credentials.
Verify tracking numbers directly on the courier's official app or bookmarked website.
recoverySteps: Call 1930 (National Cyber Crime Reporting Helpline) or log on to cybercrime.gov.in.
Immediately lock your debit/credit card via your bank app or net banking.
Contact your bank's fraud division to block further unauthorized merchant transactions.
